source.title: The reviewing of object files: Object-specific integration of information

confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily-replicated demonstration that a perceived object is a persisting FILE that is actively re-linked and updated across time, motion, and occlusion -- not a fixed one-shot binding. This grounds MECH-456's core premise ('binding is maintained-not-intrinsic'). Held below 0.7 because object-file reviewing establishes the UPDATABILITY / maintained-correspondence half of the claim strongly but speaks only obliquely to the SWITCHING half (a competitor world-configuration overtaking and forcing a re-bind); and because it is a 1992 visual-attention psychophysics result whose transfer to a latent self<->world-config binder is analogical, not measured.
failure_signatures: Object-file reviewing shows correspondence is maintained and updated across a gap, but the paradigm does not force a competitor to OVERTAKE the current file -- it is largely evidence for continuity, the opposite pole from rebinding, so it under-tests the switch trigger MECH-456 asserts.

The 'object' is an attended visual token over a brief display (hundreds of ms); MECH-456's bound thing is a self-anchored world-configuration in a trained latent architecture. Equating the two is a formal import, not a measured equivalence.
No prediction-error / competitor-support variable is manipulated; the mechanism that decides WHEN to keep vs re-link the file is not isolated here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A perceived object is represented as an 'object file' -- a temporary episodic representation that collects and integrates information about that object as it is encountered. When a later stimulus is interpreted as a new state of a previously seen object, information is reviewed and re-linked to the existing file (object-specific priming), showing that object correspondence across time, motion, and occlusion is an active, continuously-maintained process rather than a fixed one-shot binding.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the psychological ancestor of MECH-456's central premise that binding is MAINTAINED, not intrinsic. REE's cross_stream_binder holds a self-anchor <-> world-configuration binding; MECH-456 asserts that binding is continuously re-evaluated the way an object file is continuously reviewed and re-linked. Kahneman/Treisman/Gibbs establish that biological perception treats a bound entity as an updatable file whose correspondence must be actively re-computed as the input evolves -- the necessary precondition for a rebinding operation to be a real functional process rather than a static lookup.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This grounds the 'binding is an active, updatable correspondence' half of MECH-456; it does NOT evidence the specific rebinding TRIGGER (competitor-overtake under prediction error) that separates MECH-456 from mere maintenance. Object files are a visual-attention construct over brief displays; the transfer to a latent architectural binder is analogical (the claim's own 'non-formal-import' grounding), and none of REE's binder behaviour is measured by this paper.
mapping.source_context: Human visual psychophysics; object-specific priming across preview/target displays with moving and occluded objects.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (foundational, ~2000+ citations, robust and replicated). Mapping fidelity moderate: grounds updatability/maintained-correspondence tightly but the competitor-overtake switch only obliquely. Transfer risk elevated: 1992 visual-attention psychophysics -> trained latent binder is an analogy, and the timescale (sub-second attention) differs from REE's within-episode binding.
